comments.author: @nilcarborundum7001
comments.text: "Fine dining" it undoubtedly is, and fine craftsmanship too. For all that, this is the kind of cooking I actually value least - a lot of it is more for show than it is food; it is meant to impress the rich but un-hungry rather than feeding a family. I am more impressed by simple, yet elegant ways to nourish yourself and others with simple ingredients, no waste and no over-consumption. I think I prefer a bowl of a big-hearted stew full of vegetables or a rolled omelette to tiny, fancy morsels arranged on a piece of slate using tweezers or draped over antlers (so silly!), if you get my meaning. What I do greatly respect, though, is his use of locally sourced ingredients if at all possible.
